conventions: TypeScript strict throughout; no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`; prefer `readonly`, `const`, `?.` and `??` (copilot-instructions).
Use `Merge<Base, Overrides>` from `@excalidraw/common/utility-types` instead of `Omit<>&`; use `app.ownerDocument`/`app.ownerWindow` for any DOM API (AGENTS.md).
Formatting is Prettier via @excalidraw/prettier-config (double quotes, trailing commas, 80 columns); eslint runs with --max-warnings=0, so a prettier/prettier warning fails.

Imports: value imports first, then `import type` blocks (separate-type-imports); groups separated by one blank line; cross-package imports use the `@excalidraw/common`, `@excalidraw/element`, `@excalidraw/math` aliases, in-package imports are relative (`./bounds`).

Elements are immutable: every element update goes through `newElementWith(el, {...})` (which bumps the version and so invalidates ShapeCache, ElementBounds and the hit-shape cache); only test helpers mutate in place.
Comments are lowercase, short, and say why, like the existing ones in bounds.ts.
UI strings come from `t("labels.x")`; only packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json is edited; no literal text in JSX.

An element with no `arrowheadSize` (or `null`/`"medium"`) must produce exactly HEAD's geometry, bounds, shapes and SVG: scale 1 multiplies, never branches into new code, and the bounds extension runs only when the scale is above 1.

Tests are Vitest with jsdom and @testing-library/react: globals `describe`/`it`/`expect`, `vi` imported from "vitest" only when used; editor tests use `API`, `UI` and `render` from packages/excalidraw/tests/helpers and test-utils; element tests import sources relatively (`../src/bounds`).
Element snapshots must not change; only the appState snapshots gain `currentItemArrowheadSize: null`.

units.behaviour: Scale every arrowhead size computation by the element's preset, and widen linear-element bounds by the drawn heads only when the scale is above 1.
rules: 1. getArrowheadSize(arrowhead, scale = 1) keeps its switch of base sizes and returns base * scale; with no scale it returns HEAD's value.

2. getArrowheadAngle(arrowhead, size?, scale = 1): drawn size = size ?? getArrowheadSize(arrowhead, scale); for `arrow`, fullSize = getArrowheadSize(arrowhead, scale) and the widest size is ARROW_ARROWHEAD_WIDEST_SIZE * scale, so the 20-to-30 degree widening keeps its proportions; every other branch is unchanged.
3. getCardinalityMarkerScale gains a 4th parameter `scale: number` and passes it to each of its three getArrowheadSize calls.

4. getArrowheadSizeBeyondLastSegment computes `const scale = getArrowheadSizeScale(element.arrowheadSize);` first and uses it in the cardinality branch (size and marker scale), the `arrow` legibleSize and both `arrow` getArrowheadAngle calls; the other branches (bar, diamond, triangle, circle) are size-independent caps and stay as they are.

5. getArrowheadPoints computes the same scale and uses getArrowheadSize(arrowhead, scale) as `size` and getArrowheadAngle(arrowhead, minSize, scale) as `angle`; the short-segment clamp code is unchanged, so it clamps the scaled size.

6. New private helper (above getLinearElementRotatedBounds) extends a Bounds by the drawn heads: it walks start then end with the defaults shape.ts uses (`startArrowhead = null`, `endArrowhead = "arrow"` for a legacy undefined), skips a null head, and collects the parts shape.ts draws: cardinality_one_or_many = cardinality_many + cardinality_one at CARDINALITY_ONE_OR_MANY_BAR_OFFSET; cardinality_exactly_one = cardinality_one at CARDINALITY_INNER_BAR_OFFSET + cardinality_one; cardinality_zero_or_one = circle_outline at CARDINALITY_ZERO_CIRCLE_OFFSET with diameter scale CARDINALITY_ZERO_CIRCLE_SCALE + cardinality_one at CARDINALITY_INNER_BAR_OFFSET; cardinality_zero_or_many = cardinality_many + that circle_outline part; any other head is one part of its own type.

7. For each part it calls getArrowheadPoints(element, [shape], position, part, offset); a null result adds nothing; a circle result [x, y, diameter] adds the transformed center plus and minus diameter * diameterScale / 2 on both axes; a cardinality_one result adds only its bar ends (indices 2..5, the pairs generateArrowheadCardinalityOne draws); any other result adds every (x, y) pair. Points go through the same transformXY as the shaft ops before min/max.

8. getLinearElementRotatedBounds calls the helper right after `let coords` is set, only when isArrowElement(element) && getArrowheadSizeScale(element.arrowheadSize) > 1, and before the bound-text merge; lines (which never draw heads) and small/medium/absent sizes skip it, so their bounds and every hit result equal HEAD.
9. No other function changes; ElementBounds caches by version, so the head extent is computed once per element version (no per-hit-test allocation).
